open_questions: Duration 1.741x central for TIC radius (1.47x for Gaia FLAME radius) implies inflated density; positively b impacts fit but stellar-radius revision to 3.25-3.32 Rearth leaves 1.45x ratio consistent with grazing and tidal circularisation for 1.03 d period.

Phase-curve amplitude 4474 ppm (ratio_to_depth 1.091, chi2 187.8 dof 9) and variability_chi2_dof 20.86 indicate strong out-of-transit modulation, likely synchronous ellipsoidal/beaming and spots on rapidly rotating M dwarf.

Rotation period 1.0295 d equals orbital period 1.03219 d (signal_over_rotation 1.0026, sector 1 amplitude 19524 ppm, sector 28 22940 ppm) – dip is at 1x spin, which occurs by chance but requires radial-velocity mass measurement to rule out tidally locked stellar companion and resolve density mismatch.
dossier.public_summary: A steady 4100 ppm dip repeats every 1.03 days on the target M dwarf for 43 transits with no odd/even difference or secondary, giving a planet-like size of 2.8 Earth radii. The transit is flat-bottomed and steady between TESS sectors. The 1.7 hour duration is longer than expected but fits a slightly larger Gaia radius and a grazing geometry, and the large phase-curve signal matches the star’s equal 1.03 day spin – best explained as a planet around a synchronously rotating star pending mass measurements.

reasons.why: Planet-sized dip, below 10 Rearth, inconsistent with stellar eclipse on target.
No odd/even depth difference (ratio 1.2, 649.6 ppm diff), no evidence for binary at twice period.
No significant secondary (SNR 2.31, at phase 0.795) well below brightening bump SNR 7.808.
Difference imaging puts dip on target (offset 0.8294 arcsec, offset_sigma 0.1208) and rules out neighbours >3 sigma away.
Depth steady between sectors (3843 +/-410 ppm sector 1, 3853 +/-556 ppm sector 28) with only 0.2599% change, derivative of planet.
Flat-bottomed transit shape favours planet over V-shaped binary/grazing eclipse despite long duration.
